newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timber tycoon denies interest in Astra.
newsitem.headline: Timber tycoon denies interest in Astra.

text.p: Indonesian timber tycoon Mohamad "Bob" Hasan has denied he is interested in buying shares in automobile conglomerate PT Astra International, Kompas newspaper said on Saturday.
"Why is my name used in connection with Astra shares," Hasan was quoted as saying. "I do not own a single share in Astra."

Last week, Putera Sampoerna, founder and president director of cigarette manufacturer PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, effectively became the largest single shareholder in the car manufacturer with the purchase of a 12.66 percent stake.
The Bisnis Indonesia daily has reported that Sampoerna may sell his holdings in Astra to a group controlled by Hasan.
Hasan's Nusamba group is owned 80 percent by three foundations controlled by Indonesian President Suharto.
The president's eldest son Sigit Hardjojudanto and Hasan hold 10 percent each.
But Hasan denied that he had any intention of buying Astra stock.
"If people are intentionally using this issue to put up the share price then this is called insider trading," he was quoted as saying by Kompas.

Astra shares had risen sharply since rumours started circulating two weeks ago that a takeover bid was in progress. But they have fallen since and closed at 3,600 rupiah on Friday, down from a peak of 3,825 last week.
